headline_marked: US [[strikes Iranian island of Larak]] near Strait of Hormuz
headline: US strikes Iranian island of Larak near Strait of Hormuz
summary: The US military targeted two rocket launchers on the island, prompting Iran to warn of a 'strategic and deadly' mistake with severe consequences.
details: The United States military carried out a strike on Iran's Larak Island, located near the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz, on Sunday.
US officials confirmed the operation, marking the first such attack on Iranian territory in over a month.
According to CNN, the strike targeted two Iranian rocket launchers on the island as they were being prepared to lay sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced that both military personnel and civilians were killed and injured in the attack.
While the IRGC reported casualties, they have not yet released a specific number of victims.
IRGC spokesperson Sardar Mohebbi described the US action as a 'strategic and deadly' mistake, warning that the US would pay a heavy price militarily and economically.
The Trump administration stated that US Central Command (CENTCOM) had completed the removal of sea mines from international shipping routes in the waterway last week.
President Donald Trump had previously warned that any vessel attempting to lay new mines in the waterway would be destroyed immediately and according to plan.
caption:
The US has struck Larak Island in Iran. Iran warns the US has made a 'strategic and deadly' mistake.

The United States military carried out a strike on Iran's Larak Island, located near the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz, on Sunday.

US officials confirmed the operation, marking the first such attack on Iranian territory in over a month.

According to CNN, the strike targeted two Iranian rocket launchers on the island as they were being prepared to lay sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced that both military personnel and civilians were killed and injured in the attack.

While the IRGC reported casualties, they have not yet released a specific number of victims.

IRGC spokesperson Sardar Mohebbi described the US action as a 'strategic and deadly' mistake, warning that the US would pay a heavy price militarily and economically.

The Trump administration stated that US Central Command (CENTCOM) had completed the removal of sea mines from international shipping routes in the waterway last week.

President Donald Trump had previously warned that any vessel attempting to lay new mines in the waterway would be destroyed immediately and according to plan.

headline_marked: Over 3,000 missing as [[glacial collapse triggers deadly floods]] in Nepal
headline: Over 3,000 missing as glacial collapse triggers deadly floods in Nepal
summary: At least 752 bodies have been recovered after an icy torrent swept through villages, leaving thousands missing and entire settlements in ruins.
details: A massive glacial collapse on the China-Nepal border triggered a wall of water and debris that ripped through the region, leaving a trail of destruction from north to south.
Official figures from Nepal and China report that over 3,000 people are missing, while at least 752 bodies have been recovered so far.
Entire villages, such as Dhunge, which once housed 150 families, have been completely obliterated and reduced to swampy expanses of mud and debris.
Survivors are now returning to the ruins of their homes to salvage personal belongings and documents, often finding nothing but silt and wreckage.
The disaster has created a critical health crisis, with displaced persons in camps lacking essential medications for chronic conditions like diabetes and high blood pressure.
Rescue workers from groups like the Nepal Scouts report that debris remains knee-high in many areas, with the grim likelihood of more bodies buried beneath the silt.
caption:
Over 3,000 people are missing after a glacial collapse sent a wall of water and debris through Nepal.

A massive glacial collapse on the China-Nepal border triggered a wall of water and debris that ripped through the region, leaving a trail of destruction from north to south.

Official figures from Nepal and China report that over 3,000 people are missing, while at least 752 bodies have been recovered so far.

Entire villages, such as Dhunge, which once housed 150 families, have been completely obliterated and reduced to swampy expanses of mud and debris.

Survivors are now returning to the ruins of their homes to salvage personal belongings and documents, often finding nothing but silt and wreckage.

The disaster has created a critical health crisis, with displaced persons in camps lacking essential medications for chronic conditions like diabetes and high blood pressure.

Rescue workers from groups like the Nepal Scouts report that debris remains knee-high in many areas, with the grim likelihood of more bodies buried beneath the silt.
